note.question: How does demand allocation in service systems in the presence of service-fulfillment costs contribute to capacity sharing?
note.overview: The model considers capacity sharing through demand allocation among firms with multiple demand sources and multiple service facilities. Firms decide on the allocation of demand from different sources to different facilities to minimize delay costs and service-fulfillment costs possibly subject to service-level requirements. If firms decide to operate collectively as a coalition, they must also decide on a scheme for sharing the total cost.

components.formal: Objective relation: Finally, we introduce a special type of cooperative games called market games, in which players can cooperate by reallocating commitments to minimize the total cost for the system (see chapter 13 of Osborne and Rubinstein 1994).
conditions: A subset of players S, S ⊆ N is called a coalition; the largest coalition N is referred to as the grand coalition, and each coalition S is associated with a real value denoted by z(S) with z(Ø) 0.
A vector φ (φk)k∈N is called a cost allocation if φk corresponds to the portion of total expected cost in the grand coalition that is allocated to player k.
Then, a cost allocation φ is said to be a core cost allocation of the game if it is efficient and stable for any S ⊂N.
